Both stated within-group differences favor A and the pooled difference favors B. This is the descriptive strict reversal. All rates are arithmetically consistent, and observational fractions establish no individual switching effect.

0.20*60%+0.80*90%=12%+72%=84%. 72% omits the newcomer contribution; 75% uses equal weights; 80% confuses a weight with a rate.

A 50% newcomer reference weight requires a newcomer rate, but 0/0 is unavailable. Computing 45% assumes an unjustified zero rate; computing 90% assumes the experienced rate applies to newcomers; 100% has no basis.
The only positive reference weight is on experienced players, whose rate is 9/10. The excluded newcomer group contributes zero without imputing its unavailable rate, giving 90%.

A switching intervention needs a defined intervention and a causal account of assignment, timing, and common causes. Pooling, searching subgroups, or imposing equal weights does not supply missing causal identification.

Practice is allowed to lie on the method-to-success pathway, and the target explicitly includes that pathway. Conditioning on post-method practice can remove that part of the total effect; neither equal weights nor the pooled association resolves this automatically.
